## Who he is, as stated in his own posts

- Ricardo Heredia, author of the Substack "The Underdoc". The newsletter describes itself as "building AI systems, using football analytics as the sandbox" (`embrace-your-weirdness`).
- Graduated from med school in Venezuela in 2019 and felt unfulfilled (`embrace-your-weirdness`). He later describes the newsletter as "bridging medicine and tech for anyone doing the same from a different background" (`using-agentic-ides-for-football-analytics`).
- Found Python during the pandemic, applied it to football analytics, took MOOCs, networked, and joined a non-profit group of analysts working with NWSL and national teams on data from StatsBomb, Tracab and Opta (`embrace-your-weirdness`).
- His first tech role was at an AI consultancy on health projects and speech recognition (`embrace-your-weirdness`). He mentions healthcare data/AI work on his day job (`got-interviewed-by-ryan-day`).
- When he left medicine he did not know a single person working in tech (`voice-tonality.md`, on record).
- He is taking the Agentic AI Engineering course at Towards AI Academy, taught by Paul Iusztin and Louis-Francois Bouchard, and applying it to a tool he builds for himself (`got-interviewed-by-ryan-day`).
- He has been interviewed in Ryan Day's Tip Sheet issue #65 (`got-interviewed-by-ryan-day`).

## Football as a sandbox

- Football is the sandbox, never the axis (`SKILL.md`, Topic scope). The posts use football data to teach engineering: scraping Transfermarkt, using FBRef, building dashboards with free data, scouting with Driblab Pro, and a football RAG system (corpus titles).
- He started with football analytics because he wanted to apply what he was learning to something he cared about and found fun (`got-interviewed-by-ryan-day`).
- He lost track of time building his football RAG system one Saturday, working from 9pm to 3am, and said "It felt like craft" (`embrace-your-weirdness`).
- Conversational AI, voice and healthtech are in scope as patterns only (`SKILL.md`).

## How he sounds

- Conversational and direct, like talking to a technical friend. Contractions, fillers like "like", casual counts. Small ESL quirks are part of the voice (`voice-tonality.md`).
